data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Arisina was an epithet of the goddess Helios, the Sun. Her name means 'Elevated by the Sun' or 'Shining One'. In Christianity, Arisina can be interpreted as a symbol of the Resurrected Christ, who rises above all with the power of the sun. The name Arisina carries the meaning “Elevated by the sun” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Arisina usually hope their child will grow to embody elevated by the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Arisina, a town in ancient Phrygia, was known as a major center for early Christianity. It was the site of one of the Seven Churches of Revelation, identified as Smyrna. The town was significant in the early spread of Christianity in Anatolia and was a target of Roman persecution.

Arisina, a medieval village in the region of Calabria, Italy, was a significant center of Greek Orthodox Christianity. It was the site of a major monastic community, the Arsinian Monastery, which was a center of learning and pilgrimage. The village was destroyed during the Ottoman conquest of Calabria in the late 15th century.
